question.question: Does RawNode.Status preserve the installed implicit-joint AutoLeave policy when copying tracker.Config, as required by the copy/status interfaces?
question.importance: Incorrect configuration introspection can misdescribe whether Raft or the application owns joint-exit initiation. This is a local reporting responsibility connected to active membership, not an established safety violation or persistence consequence.
contexts: Live legally applied implicit joint configuration before its normal automatic exit
Detached status copy of the same node, with no intervening protocol operation
event_paths: Actual joint configuration commit -> ApplyConfChange returns ConfState -> RawNode.Status -> getStatus -> Config.Clone

supporting_behavior_ids.B-replication: Establishes actual committed configuration entry under current voting rules.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-application: Caller applies the committed entry before observing status; Advance may subsequently trigger exit.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-client: Public status observation and application ordering.

counterevidence: Map-valued membership fields are copied and live configuration is not mutated.
Changer.EnterJoint resets AutoLeave from its argument, LeaveJoint clears it intentionally and Simple rejects joint configuration; those paths do not establish unintended live policy loss.
Previously observed false AutoLeave came from the export copy while live AutoLeave stayed true.
question.trigger_rationale: Clone explicitly promises a copy, yet its return literal omits AutoLeave; getStatus directly uses it. A small paired public observation at real ApplyConfChange can test the responsibility without relying on a synthetic config or hypothesized external persistence consumer.

obligation.description: A Status configuration copy of an installed tracker configuration must preserve its AutoLeave value at the observation point, without changing the original configuration.

scope.description: RawNode.Status in a serialized crash-free instance immediately after applying a genuinely committed implicit joint change, before further state-machine operations.
assumptions: No concurrent mutation during Status call.
excluded: No claim that external applications persist or act on the incorrect status.
No claim of live policy mutation or quorum-safety failure.

grounding.derivation: Config.Clone promises a copy sharing no memory; preserving scalar policy is part of copying the Config, not merely copying its maps. Status describes the current peer view and getStatus assigns that clone without a documented lossy transformation. AutoLeave is an explicit Config semantic field.
grounding.applicability: Same node, same installed configuration and serialized observation; compare returned ApplyConfChange ConfState with Status before Advance changes anything.
alternatives: The Changer call sites intentionally override AutoLeave; this does not justify an undocumented loss in status export.

bindings.description: Copies configuration for status and Changer; scalar AutoLeave is absent from returned literal.

associations.rationale: Explicit copy responsibility applies to the automatic-exit policy field.
Connects clone behavior to the public status observation.
